question: Does the conformance and acceptance oracle validly and reliably measure what it claims?

required_evidence: populated TASK_RULE_MATRIX and TASK_ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX; oracle_result and acceptance_result artifacts; mutation tests
notes: addresses v1 missing acceptance oracle and constant layer_jaccard; dependency-direction reference checker + synthetic fixtures implemented (necessary not sufficient for G1); pilot task candidates authored with hidden manifests in a separate private evaluator repo (status review; not frozen); task-specific oracle validity + hidden-acceptance validation remain open; Suite-classification decision D: PT06 is functional-only (a valid primary functional candidate, structurally excluded from E1); the pre-run opportunity reassessment additionally makes PT05 functional-only (functionally valid but structurally ineligible for E1 because its required functional work creates no currently scored dependency-direction opportunity - a construct/feasibility reclassification decided before any benchmark or model execution, never a model outcome, never zero violations and never a failed run) so only PT01-PT04 remain E1-scored candidates and NO reserve was activated to restore the count; DECISION B (TD-B34) records that the current active task set does not sample enough distinct dependency-direction decisions for confirmatory inference and that additional public architecture tasks must be authored before Stage 0 - G1 therefore remains BLOCKING and the suite is NOT ready; PR02 remains blocked and inactive because its terminal-state completion criterion is not externally reachable at the source substrate (TD-B26) and must not be promoted until repaired and independently re-approved; PR01 remains an inactive reserve; only dependency-direction opportunities (AR-DEP-001..006) are currently scored into E1, so G1 oracle validity for E1 means dependency-direction validity - CON-ACB rules are unimplemented stubs that must never report PASS.

question: Do the tasks and reset checkpoints discriminate between conditions without floor/ceiling saturation?
pass_criterion: pilot shows non-degenerate variation across conditions and reset states; checkpoints leave meaningful post-reset work
required_evidence: pilot runs (paid; NOT part of this work package); dispersion and ceiling checks
notes: guards against saturated metrics (v1 ci_pass all True); condition-neutral checkpoints (TD-B01); interaction-focused power simulation before the core grid (TD-B20); pilot task candidates + draft condition-neutral reset checkpoints authored; discrimination untested (no pilot run); Suite-classification decision D: the repeated frozen opportunities collapse onto a small number of shared boundary decisions, so pseudo-replication must be modelled in the power simulation (TD-B30) and a floor effect is plausible; the model-visible source comments that explicitly revealed some scored dependency rules to C1 have been REMOVED and the worktree leakage sweep now reads source comments and refuses a snapshot that states a rule (TD-B23 and TD-B24 both resolved before any benchmark or model execution; the edit was comment-only and proven non-behavioural, and api->core, infra->core and features->infra remain structurally detectable), so the baseline is no longer partly guided by prose - the floor-effect risk from that source is removed, though floor effects from the shared-boundary collapse below remain untested. The pre-run opportunity reassessment additionally makes G2 BLOCKING for a construct-coverage reason: after PT05's reclassification only PT01-PT04 remain E1-scored candidates and they do not sample enough DISTINCT dependency-direction decisions for confirmatory inference - task count is not the independent architecture-decision count and repeated exposures to one boundary are clustered - so additional public architecture tasks must be authored before Stage 0 (DECISION B; TD-B34) and the final power simulation must wait until those distinct decisions exist and are approved (TD-B37). No power value is frozen and the suite is NOT ready.

question: Is there a direct AFCI effect on a direct conformance or completeness outcome (C4 vs C1)?
pass_criterion: pre-registered confirmatory contrast per the SAP with multiplicity-corrected inference and a reported effect size with 95% CI
required_evidence: frozen result set; SAP-specified model fit
notes: thresholds not derived from v1 (TD-B07); interaction power simulation (TD-B20). Suite-classification decision D: the single primary endpoint is the dependency-direction violation rate per applicable frozen opportunity (E1; D8 as narrowed; SAP 2.1) and it measures layered dependency-direction conformance ONLY - it is never reported as broad or general architectural conformance (G8). The primary C4-versus-C1 contrast uses numerator opportunity_accounting.violated_opportunity_count and offset opportunity_accounting.applicable_opportunity_count; applicable_rule_count is NOT an admissible offset and a per-rule denominator is prohibited. The contrast is fitted over structurally eligible scored tasks ONLY (e1_analysis_eligibility=scored; currently PT01-PT04): PT06 is functional-only and must NOT enter the G3 E1 contrast, PT05 is now functional-only by the pre-run opportunity reassessment and must NOT enter it either, and PR01/PR02 are inactive reserves that must NOT enter it either. E1 is computed from the PRODUCTION dependency graph only: test specs, test support material and tooling/config TypeScript are partitioned out before any import edge is built, so they can never enter the numerator and can never move the frozen denominator. The final interaction power simulation must NOT be run on the current four-task architecture set: task count is not the independent architecture-decision count, repeated exposures to one boundary are clustered, and no final power value is frozen (TD-B34/TD-B37). Applicable-frozen-opportunity satisfaction (E2) is a descriptive transformation of the same measurement, not an independent confirmatory contrast.

question: Is the architecture guard validated (alias-aware; precision and recall; mutation tests)?
pass_criterion: precision and recall meet a pre-registered bar on a labelled corpus; seeded @afci-bench/* alias and barrel-laundered violations are detected; known-good diverse solutions are not flagged
required_evidence: labelled violation/clean corpus (seeded incl alias/barrel-laundered); alias+barrel+re-export resolution; moved/deleted-code + full-repository (not added-line-only) evaluation; known-good diverse-solution specificity; legitimate alternatives frozen before confirmatory data; blinded double rating >=0.70 for manual rules; guard_result artifacts; mutation tests
notes: v1 guard matched literal libs/* and was blind to @afci-bench/* aliases (total=0); v2 oracle implements alias/barrel/re-export + moved/deleted + full-repo eval with synthetic fixtures; labelled corpus + mutation + inter-rater pending; Suite-classification decision D adds required G6 evidence: validation of the opportunity-attribution mechanism - TD-B27. The mechanism is now SCOPE-BASED (an opportunity is scored over its frozen architectural scope, locator.importer_path is provenance only) and the public M0-M7 mutation corpus (experiments/v2/oracle/tests/scopeAttribution.test.ts) shows violations introduced in NEW files, in moved files and after anchor deletion are attributed to the frozen opportunity instead of being missed by the E1 numerator; STILL REQUIRED for G6: the same attribution validated on the labelled corpus against the pre-registered precision/recall bar, known-good and mutation cases in new files extended to the labelled corpus, and re-authored private per-task opportunity sets; AR-DEP-001 considered for all private manifests so relevant dependency-family violations are not silently omitted (TD-B28). The existing false-positive/false-negative, alias/barrel/re-export, moved/deleted, known-good-specificity and blinded-double-rating requirements are RETAINED, not replaced. G6 additionally requires validation under the PRODUCTION-SOURCE policy: E1 is computed from the production dependency graph only and test specs, test support material and tooling/build configuration TypeScript are partitioned out before any import edge is built, so the labelled corpus and every private frozen opportunity set must be re-checked to confirm no opportunity depends on a test-only or config-only dependency and no seeded violation sits in an excluded file (TD-B36). The public M8-A to M8-F mutation cases regression-lock the policy but do NOT discharge G6, which remains BLOCKING.

question: Before any claim is marked supported does each have its direct metric and evidence with no over-claim?
pass_criterion: every promoted claim has its required evidence; no claim marked supported without it; architectural integrity (CON-AI) not claimed as directly measured
notes: guardrail against architectural-integrity over-claim; Suite-classification decision D: G8 additionally PROHIBITS any claim that broader architectural dimensions were directly measured by E1. E1 measures layered dependency-direction conformance only; contract ownership, port/interface placement, observability completeness, duplicated logic and general business-logic placement are CON-ACB secondary/manual evidence whose confirmatory use requires Cohen's kappa >= 0.70. The paper must not describe E1 as broad or general architectural conformance, and E1 exclusions (PT05/PT06 functional-only; PR01/PR02 inactive reserves) must be reported rather than presented as null results, and a structurally ineligible task must never be presented as zero violations, failed, missing, invalid or a refusal.
